articleBody:
- [ ] Checked ceiling plane across the upper cabinets with a level — Identifies dips that require a two-piece crown and backer system rather than a single rigid molding.
- [ ] Measured vertical plumb along adjacent walls and corners — Tells you exactly how much scribe allowance is needed on cabinet filler strips to eliminate gaps.
- [ ] Inspected factory finish and color match on all molding stock — Confirms that crown, light rail, and toe-kicks match your cabinet door dye lots before anyone makes a cut.
- [ ] Verified acclimation of solid wood trim inside the room — Prevents shrinkage, miters opening up, or joints cracking after heating or air conditioning cycles run.
- [ ] Confirmed sub-fascia backing blocks are installed above upper boxes — Gives crown molding a solid wooden nailing surface so fasteners do not penetrate interior cabinet boxes.
- [ ] Verified toe-kick skins cover all leveling shims and box seams — Ensures a continuous, clean base that seals cabinet bottoms against spills and floor debris.
- [ ] Checked light-rail depth against under-cabinet fixture profiles — Ensures under-cabinet task lighting remains completely hidden from seated sightlines across the room.
- [ ] Tested corner angles with an adjustable miter gauge — Prevents mismatched 45-degree joints caused by out-of-square 90-degree drywall corners.

How to use this checklist:
Review this list right after your cabinet boxes are anchored and before your finish carpenter starts cutting profile molding. Catching out-of-square framing or missing nailers early saves expensive decorative wood stock from being ruined.
